<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Load ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 token embeddings without treating their scale tensors as unexpected weights. Rebased onto `3f45273050ac38b705eeac9c1e4d5e5f0330034c` and simplified the original implementation.

## Claims

- Support row-major per-tensor FP8 and packed NVFP4 input embeddings, including mixed-policy `W4A16_NVFP4`; dequantize only selected rows to the model dtype.
- Keep output heads on main's existing linear path. Preserve exclusions and unquantized fallbacks; reject unsupported tied input/output embeddings explicitly.
- Reuse `VocabParallelEmbedding` metadata, remove unreachable fused-projection handling, and consolidate duplicated tests around real layer constructors. The quantization addition is reduced from 246 to 168 lines.
- Document enablement and limitations and wire the focused regressions into an H200 CI step.

## Validation

Validation uses a GB300, Python 3.12, PyTorch `2.14.0+cu132`, and Transformers `5.20.2` with the rebased Python source. The initial run used main `c13d4a5a4` with the published wheel from its immediate parent `af6665b5dd2098898dce52b9e1c5005863738024` (identical compiled sources). Main then advanced to `3f4527305`; the final feature verification uses that Python source with the same wheel. The intervening native MXFP4/HiSparse changes are outside these embedding, dense Llama, and NVFP4 test paths; they are not validated here.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -q \
  -k 'embedding and not checkpoint' --tb=short
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -q \
  -k test_modelopt_embedding_checkpoint --tb=short
```

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Real-layer lookup, dtype/shape/padding, policy exclusion, LM-head dispatch, tied-weight rejection | 46 passed |
| LLM checkpoint generation compared with BF16 controls | 3 passed; FP8, NVFP4, and W4A16_NVFP4 produce identical greedy tokens to their controls |
| Regression on unmodified ModelOpt/Llama code | Fails as expected: no parameter named `embed_tokens.input_scale` (the relevant base files are unchanged through `3f4527305`) |
| Final-main repeat (`-k embedding`) | 49 passed in 143.23s |
| Existing Nemotron-H checkpoint smoke test | Baseline, FP8, and W4A16_NVFP4 embedding variants: 3 prompts each generated with finite log probabilities; quantized variants used the intended embedding methods |
| GitHub Actions / Read the Docs | Blocked by repository pre-run eligibility gate; actual CI lint/docs build did not start. DCO passed. |
| All applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy and CI test tethering | Passed |

The checkpoint tests use locally constructed tiny Llama checkpoints with real serialized tensors and greedy generation. The larger smoke test uses an existing local Nemotron-H export with separate, locally quantized embedding variants; other weights are retained. These are correctness/smoke checks, not a language-model accuracy evaluation. Current validation supersedes the old branch's historical checkpoint results; full accuracy evaluation and non-CUDA platforms are not claimed.

## Details

```text
embedding token IDs -> gather quantized rows -> dequantize to model dtype
lm_head            -> existing ModelOpt linear method
```

FP8 scaling now happens in FP32 before casting to the layer's configured dtype. NVFP4 lookup retains the checkpoint's row-indexable packing and avoids GEMM repacking; empty and scalar inputs preserve their shapes. `input_scale` remains accepted for checkpoint compatibility and is not applied during lookup.

This does not duplicate #45535 (compressed-tensors embedding formats) or #48870 (fused tied-weight output projection). The earlier related #35660 is closed. Related ModelOpt export work: NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#1495. Main already contains the Nemotron-H embedding config/prefix wiring, so no additional Nemotron model diff is needed.

The remote pre-run gate requires a verified/ready label or at least four merged author PRs (GitHub reports zero); the actual Actions lint job is skipped. Read the Docs exits from `docs/pre_run_check.sh` on that same gate before building docs. See [failed gate](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/40403469484) and [docs build](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35425836/). No retry or label request was made.

The ModelOpt feature page documents this user-visible addition. The repository release process does not require a separate per-PR changelog file. AI assistance (Claude and OpenAI Codex) was used; human submitter review remains required under the contribution policy.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses the embedding layer's metadata and existing NVFP4 dequantization; leaves core scheduling and runner code untouched.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** 49 final-main GPU tests, before/after regression evidence, and real-checkpoint generation completed. CI eligibility gate and binary/source boundary are documented.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Applicable hooks pass; documentation and CI selection are updated.

## GSM8K embedding-only accuracy

Validated one complete pass of the **1,319-question GSM8K test split per format**. Each run has 1,319 unique successful model responses matched to its scored outputs, parsed reasoning and extractable final answers throughout. Per format: **0/1,319 request timeouts, terminal runtime/scoring failures, truncated outputs, empty final answers or missing questions**; zero retries or cache-replayed responses. All wrong answers remain in the score denominator. Small startup canaries are excluded.

The control uses **BF16 embeddings in the supplied mixed-precision 24GB model**. The body and output head are identical across all three runs; this is **not a whole-model BF16 comparison**.

| Embeddings | Correct | Accuracy | Accuracy 95% CI (%) | Change vs control (pp) | Change 95% CI (pp) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 (control) | 1276/1319 | 96.74% | [95.64, 97.57] | — | — |
| FP8 E4M3 | 1267/1319 | 96.06% | [94.87, 96.98] | -0.68 | [-1.36, 0.00] |
| NVFP4 W4A16 | 1268/1319 | 96.13% | [94.95, 97.05] | -0.61 | [-1.29, 0.00] |

Accuracy intervals use Wilson's method. Change intervals use a paired bootstrap over the same questions (20,000 resamples, seed 42791). These are question-level intervals from **one generation per question**, and do not estimate seed-to-seed generation variability. No pass/fail accuracy threshold was applied; these measurements do not establish broad accuracy equivalence.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and validation details</summary>

- PR commit: `c2a177504a1ef677f24b78dcc95bc9171041c376`.
- Model: [`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB), revision `cf2effc5c4b794ee9fb8d34eab3d1d65ce64142f`. Non-embedding weights were preserved and source shards checksum-verified.
- Dataset: OpenAI `grade-school-math`, revision `3101c7d5072418e28b9008a6636bde82a006892c`, `test`; native NeMo Skills preparation.
- Harness: NeMo Skills 26.03, native `generic/math` **zero-shot** prompt and symbolic math scorer. Added the missing `ns_gsm8k` framework registration; prompt/scoring logic unchanged. Canonical metric: `results.tasks.gsm8k.metrics.pass@1.scores.symbolic_correct.value`; verified against all recorded correctness flags.
- Generation: native chat template; thinking enabled, `medium_effort=false`; temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, seed 42; context 262,144; no additional output-token cap; explicit native `inference.timeout=43200` seconds; concurrency 16. Normalized prompts, request payloads and serving/evaluation settings match across formats apart from variant identifiers.
- Serving: one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q 96GB per run, TP=1, `--enforce-eager`, b12x linear/MoE backends, FlashInfer attention/Mamba, FP8 KV cache with explicit 32GiB allocation, `nemotron_v3` reasoning parser. Separate diagnostic deployments are excluded from accuracy.
- Reviewed diagnostics: all formats emitted a checkpoint configuration-docstring diagnostic and TorchDynamo recompile-limit warnings, with no runtime/scoring failure. The framework also warns that generic timeout/retry fields are absent from its command template; native `inference.timeout=43200` was explicitly verified in the executed command. Every scored response ended with `finish_reason=stop`; no KV preemptions were observed.
- External sanity reference: **externally unverified**. No matching GSM8K score was found in the exact model card or [Artificial Analysis model page](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/nemotron-3-5-bolt-74b-a9b/). Published whole-model precision comparisons are not used as embedding-only deltas.

This is a GSM8K regression measurement; broader reasoning/code benchmark conclusions remain untested here.

</details>

## Code Review

This pull request introduces support for quantized embeddings (FP8 and NVFP4) in the ModelOpt quantization framework, including new embedding methods and dispatch logic for VocabParallelEmbedding. Feedback identifies a potential issue where ParallelLMHead might be incorrectly excluded from quantization due to strict type checking, which could cause loading failures. Additionally, a type promotion issue in the FP8 embedding calculation was noted, where the output might inadvertently remain in float32 instead of the target model data type.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The logic here uses `type(layer) is VocabParallelEmbedding` to strictly exclude subclasses like `ParallelLMHead`. The comment states that `ParallelLMHead` is handled by the linear path. However, `ParallelLMHead` does not inherit from `LinearBase` (it inherits from `VocabParallelEmbedding`), so it will not be caught by the `isinstance(layer, LinearBase)` check at line 211. Consequently, `ParallelLMHead` will fall through to return `None` and default to `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`. If the checkpoint contains quantized weights for the LM head, this will lead to a loading failure or incorrect results during sampling. Please ensure `ParallelLMHead` is correctly routed to a quantization method that can handle its weights, especially since it is often tied to the embedding layer.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The multiplication by `layer.weight_scale` (which is a `float32` parameter) will promote the result to `float32`, potentially ignoring the desired `self.out_dtype` (usually `float16` or `bfloat16` in vLLM). This can lead to type mismatches in subsequent operations or unnecessary memory usage/performance overhead. The result should be explicitly cast back to `self.out_dtype`.

```suggestion
        return (rows.to(torch.float32) * layer.weight_scale).to(self.out_dtype)
```

+class ModelOptFp8EmbeddingMethod(QuantizeMethodBase):
+    """FP8 weight-only embedding for ModelOpt checkpoints.
+
+    Layout (per VocabParallelEmbedding partition):
+        weight        float8_e4m3fn, [vocab_per_partition, hidden]
+        weight_scale  float32,       per-tensor
+        input_scale   float32,       per-tensor (loaded but unused —
+                                      no activation to quantize)
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, quant_config: ModelOptFp8Config) -> None:
+        self.quant_config = quant_config
+        self.out_dtype = torch.get_default_dtype()
+
+    def create_weights(
+        self,
+        layer: torch.nn.Module,
+        input_size_per_partition: int,
+        output_partition_sizes: list[int],
+        input_size: int,
+        output_size: int,
+        params_dtype: torch.dtype,
+        **extra_weight_attrs,
+    ):
+        del input_size, output_size
+        output_size_per_partition = sum(output_partition_sizes)
+        weight_loader = extra_weight_attrs.get("weight_loader")
+        layer.logical_widths = output_partition_sizes
+        layer.input_size_per_partition = input_size_per_partition
+        layer.output_size_per_partition = output_size_per_partition
+
+        weight_dtype = (
+            torch.float8_e4m3fn
+            if self.quant_config.is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized
+            else params_dtype
+        )
+        weight = ModelWeightParameter(
+            data=torch.empty(
+                output_size_per_partition,
+                input_size_per_partition,
+                dtype=weight_dtype,
+            ),
+            input_dim=1,
+            output_dim=0,
+            weight_loader=weight_loader,
+        )
+        layer.register_parameter("weight", weight)
+
+        if self.quant_config.is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized:
+            weight_scale = PerTensorScaleParameter(
+                data=torch.empty(len(output_partition_sizes), dtype=torch.float32),
+                weight_loader=weight_loader,
+            )
+            weight_scale[:] = torch.finfo(torch.float32).min
+            layer.register_parameter("weight_scale", weight_scale)
+            # input_scale is accepted (so the loader sees the same key set
+            # as the linear path) but unused in embedding().
+            input_scale = PerTensorScaleParameter(
+                data=torch.empty(len(output_partition_sizes), dtype=torch.float32),
+                weight_loader=weight_loader,
+            )
+            input_scale[:] = torch.finfo(torch.float32).min
+            layer.register_parameter("input_scale", input_scale)
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        weight = layer.weight
+        max_w_scale = layer.weight_scale.max()
+        if not (layer.weight_scale == layer.weight_scale[0]).all():
+            max_w_scale, weight = requantize_with_max_scale(
+                layer.weight, layer.weight_scale, layer.logical_widths
+            )
+        # Keep weight as [vocab, hidden] — no transpose (unlike the linear
+        # path), since torch.embedding gathers along dim 0.
+        layer.weight = Parameter(weight, requires_grad=False)
+        layer.weight_scale = Parameter(max_w_scale, requires_grad=False)
+        if hasattr(layer, "input_scale") and layer.input_scale is not None:
+            layer.input_scale = Parameter(layer.input_scale.max(), requires_grad=False)
+
+    def embedding(self, layer: torch.nn.Module, input_: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        rows = torch.embedding(layer.weight, input_)
+        return rows.to(self.out_dtype) * layer.weight_scale

 For per-tensor `FP8`, vLLM converts E4M3FN weights and scales to E4M3FNUZ
 when required by the GPU, for example on AMD MI300.
 
+### Token embedding quantization
+
+ModelOpt token embeddings (`embed_tokens`) support weight-only lookup with
+per-tensor `FP8` or packed `NVFP4` weights. Mixed-precision checkpoints can also
+select `W4A16_NVFP4` for embeddings through `quantized_layers`. vLLM keeps the
+table quantized and dequantizes only the selected rows to the model dtype.
+Embedding lookup does not quantize activations or use a GEMM backend.
+
+Support is enabled automatically by the checkpoint quantization configuration.
+For a mixed-precision checkpoint, include the embedding's full module name,
+such as `model.embed_tokens`, in `quantized_layers` and remove it from
+`exclude_modules`. Excluded embeddings and embeddings absent from a
+mixed-precision policy retain their original precision. Uniform
+`FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN`, `FP8_PB_WO`, and `W4A16_NVFP4` configurations
+leave embeddings unquantized. The output `lm_head` uses the linear
+quantization path independently of the input embedding.
+
+Quantized input embeddings require `tie_word_embeddings=False`. Tying a packed
+embedding table to an output projection is unsupported and raises an error
+at load time; keep tied embeddings unquantized.
+
 For Qwen3-based DFlash and DSpark drafts, `quantized_layers` and exclusion lists
 use the exported checkpoint's module names. vLLM maps these names to the draft's
 module prefix and decoder layer indices before constructing quantized layers.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("algorithm", ["FP8", "NVFP4", "W4A16_NVFP4"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", [(6,), (2, 3), (), (0,)])
+def test_modelopt_embedding_lookup(dist_init, algorithm, dtype, shape):
+    """Real embedding loading preserves lookup values, padding, shape and dtype."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.modelopt import (
+        ModelOptFp8EmbeddingMethod,
+        ModelOptNvFp4EmbeddingMethod,
+    )
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils import (
+        dequantize_to_dtype,
+    )
+
+    config = _mixed_precision_config(
+        {"model.embed_tokens": {"quant_algo": algorithm, "group_size": 16}}
+    )
+    vocab, hidden = 65, 64
+    with torch.device("cuda"):
+        layer = VocabParallelEmbedding(
+            vocab,
+            hidden,
+            params_dtype=dtype,
+            quant_config=config,
+            prefix="model.embed_tokens",
+        )
+        if algorithm == "FP8":
+            weight = torch.arange(vocab * hidden).reshape(vocab, hidden)
+            weight = ((weight % 31 - 15).float() / 4).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+            scale = torch.tensor(0.137, dtype=torch.float32)
+            expected = (weight.float() * scale).to(dtype)
+            parameters = {"weight": weight, "weight_scale": scale}
+            assert isinstance(layer.quant_method, ModelOptFp8EmbeddingMethod)
+        else:
+            weight = (torch.arange(vocab * hidden // 2) % 256).to(torch.uint8)
+            weight = weight.reshape(vocab, hidden // 2)
+            scale = torch.full((vocab, hidden // 16), 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+            global_scale = torch.tensor(0.137, dtype=torch.float32)
+            expected = dequantize_to_dtype(
+                weight,
+                scale,
+                global_scale,
+                dtype=dtype,
+                swizzle=False,
+            )
+            parameters = {
+                "weight": weight,
+                "weight_scale": scale,
+                "weight_scale_2": global_scale,
+            }
+            assert isinstance(layer.quant_method, ModelOptNvFp4EmbeddingMethod)
+        # input_scale is deliberately non-unit: an embedding must ignore it.
+        parameters["input_scale"] = torch.tensor(7.0)

+def test_modelopt_embedding_checkpoint(tmp_path, monkeypatch, vllm_runner, algorithm):

+    from transformers import LlamaConfig, LlamaForCausalLM

+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.nvfp4_emulation_utils import (

+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT", "1")
+    config = LlamaConfig(num_hidden_layers=1, **_TINY_MODEL_CONFIG)
+    with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        model = LlamaForCausalLM(config).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    weights = dict(model.state_dict())
+    name = "model.embed_tokens"
+    original = weights[f"{name}.weight"]
+    if algorithm == "FP8":
+        _pack_fp8_weight(weights, name, algorithm)
+        dequantized = (
+            weights[f"{name}.weight"].float() * weights[f"{name}.weight_scale"]
+        ).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    else:
+        # Every nibble represents a finite FP4 value; the control uses the same
+        # saved table, fully dequantized, while inference must gather packed rows.
+        packed = (torch.arange(original.numel() // 2) % 256).to(torch.uint8)
+        packed = packed.reshape(original.shape[0], original.shape[1] // 2)
+        scale = torch.full((original.shape[0], original.shape[1] // 16), 0.5)
+        scale = scale.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        global_scale = torch.tensor(0.01)
+        weights.update(
+            {
+                f"{name}.weight": packed,
+                f"{name}.weight_scale": scale,
+                f"{name}.weight_scale_2": global_scale,
+            }
+        )
+        dequantized = dequantize_to_dtype(
+            packed,
+            scale,
+            global_scale,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            swizzle=False,
+        )
+    metadata: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "quant_method": "modelopt",
+        "quant_algo": "MIXED_PRECISION",
+        "kv_cache_quant_algo": None,
+        "exclude_modules": [],
+        "quantized_layers": {name: {"quant_algo": algorithm, "group_size": 16}},
+    }
+    outputs = []
+    for quantized in (False, True):
+        model_path = tmp_path / ("quantized" if quantized else "control")
+        if quantized:
+            model.config.quantization_config = metadata
+            state = dict(weights)
+        else:
+            state = dict(model.state_dict())
+            state[f"{name}.weight"] = dequantized
+        model.save_pretrained(model_path, state_dict=state)
+        with vllm_runner(

+            max_model_len=32,
+            max_num_seqs=1,
+            kv_cache_memory_bytes=16 << 20,
+        ) as llm:

+                llm.generate(
+                    [[1, 2, 3]],
+                    SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=4, ignore_eos=True),
+                )[0][0][0]
+            )
+    assert len(outputs[0]) == 7
+    assert outputs[1] == outputs[0]

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The logic here uses `type(layer) is VocabParallelEmbedding` to strictly exclude subclasses like `ParallelLMHead`. The comment states that `ParallelLMHead` is handled by the linear path. However, `ParallelLMHead` does not inherit from `LinearBase` (it inherits from `VocabParallelEmbedding`), so it will not be caught by the `isinstance(layer, LinearBase)` check at line 211. Consequently, `ParallelLMHead` will fall through to return `None` and default to `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`. If the checkpoint contains quantized weights for the LM head, this will lead to a loading failure or incorrect results during sampling. Please ensure `ParallelLMHead` is correctly routed to a quantization method that can handle its weights, especially since it is often tied to the embedding layer.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The multiplication by `layer.weight_scale` (which is a `float32` parameter) will promote the result to `float32`, potentially ignoring the desired `self.out_dtype` (usually `float16` or `bfloat16` in vLLM). This can lead to type mismatches in subsequent operations or unnecessary memory usage/performance overhead. The result should be explicitly cast back to `self.out_dtype`.

```suggestion
        return (rows.to(torch.float32) * layer.weight_scale).to(self.out_dtype)
```

+    Layout (per VocabParallelEmbedding partition):

+        input_size_per_partition: int,
+        output_partition_sizes: list[int],

+        weight = ModelWeightParameter(

## GSM8K embedding-only accuracy

Validated one complete pass of the **1,319-question GSM8K test split per format**. Each run has 1,319 unique successful model responses matched to its scored outputs, parsed reasoning and extractable final answers throughout. Per format: **0/1,319 request timeouts, terminal runtime/scoring failures, truncated outputs, empty final answers or missing questions**; zero retries or cache-replayed responses. All wrong answers remain in the score denominator. Small startup canaries are excluded.

The control uses **BF16 embeddings in the supplied mixed-precision 24GB model**. The body and output head are identical across all three runs; this is **not a whole-model BF16 comparison**.

| Embeddings | Correct | Accuracy | Accuracy 95% CI (%) | Change vs control (pp) | Change 95% CI (pp) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 (control) | 1276/1319 | 96.74% | [95.64, 97.57] | — | — |
| FP8 E4M3 | 1267/1319 | 96.06% | [94.87, 96.98] | -0.68 | [-1.36, 0.00] |
| NVFP4 W4A16 | 1268/1319 | 96.13% | [94.95, 97.05] | -0.61 | [-1.29, 0.00] |

Accuracy intervals use Wilson's method. Change intervals use a paired bootstrap over the same questions (20,000 resamples, seed 42791). These are question-level intervals from **one generation per question**, and do not estimate seed-to-seed generation variability. No pass/fail accuracy threshold was applied; these measurements do not establish broad accuracy equivalence.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and validation details</summary>

- PR commit: `c2a177504a1ef677f24b78dcc95bc9171041c376`.
- Model: [`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB), revision `cf2effc5c4b794ee9fb8d34eab3d1d65ce64142f`. Non-embedding weights were preserved and source shards checksum-verified.
- Dataset: OpenAI `grade-school-math`, revision `3101c7d5072418e28b9008a6636bde82a006892c`, `test`; native NeMo Skills preparation.
- Harness: NeMo Skills 26.03, native `generic/math` **zero-shot** prompt and symbolic math scorer. Added the missing `ns_gsm8k` framework registration; prompt/scoring logic unchanged. Canonical metric: `results.tasks.gsm8k.metrics.pass@1.scores.symbolic_correct.value`; verified against all recorded correctness flags.
- Generation: native chat template; thinking enabled, `medium_effort=false`; temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, seed 42; context 262,144; no additional output-token cap; explicit native `inference.timeout=43200` seconds; concurrency 16. Normalized prompts, request payloads and serving/evaluation settings match across formats apart from variant identifiers.
- Serving: one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q 96GB per run, TP=1, `--enforce-eager`, b12x linear/MoE backends, FlashInfer attention/Mamba, FP8 KV cache with explicit 32GiB allocation, `nemotron_v3` reasoning parser. Separate diagnostic deployments are excluded from accuracy.
- Reviewed diagnostics: all formats emitted a checkpoint configuration-docstring diagnostic and TorchDynamo recompile-limit warnings, with no runtime/scoring failure. The framework also warns that generic timeout/retry fields are absent from its command template; native `inference.timeout=43200` was explicitly verified in the executed command. Every scored response ended with `finish_reason=stop`; no KV preemptions were observed.
- External sanity reference: **externally unverified**. No matching GSM8K score was found in the exact model card or [Artificial Analysis model page](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/nemotron-3-5-bolt-74b-a9b/). Published whole-model precision comparisons are not used as embedding-only deltas.

This is a GSM8K regression measurement; broader reasoning/code benchmark conclusions remain untested here.

</details>

## Code Review

This pull request introduces support for quantized embeddings (FP8 and NVFP4) in the ModelOpt quantization framework, including new embedding methods and dispatch logic for VocabParallelEmbedding. Feedback identifies a potential issue where ParallelLMHead might be incorrectly excluded from quantization due to strict type checking, which could cause loading failures. Additionally, a type promotion issue in the FP8 embedding calculation was noted, where the output might inadvertently remain in float32 instead of the target model data type.
